questions.q: In Forer’s 1948 experiment, how did 39 students rate a reading that was the same for all of them?
questions.do: Take the test, then read Now the truth.
questions.a: 4.30 out of 5 on average. The text came from a newsstand astrology book.

questions.q: Why do statements beginning “At times you…” feel accurate?
questions.a: They cover both sides of a trait, so they are true of almost everyone.

questions.q: Name one thing a reader can do to seem to know you without any special power.
questions.do: Read If a person seemed to know you.
questions.a: Any of: watching your reactions, asking questions that sound like statements, guessing broadly and letting you fill in details, or remembering hits and forgetting misses (cold reading).

questions.q: Did the page use your name, birthday or colour to make your reading?
questions.do: Take the test with two different names and compare.
questions.a: No. Everyone gets the same twelve statements.

questions.q: What three questions protect you from a convincing reading?
questions.do: Read the list at the end of If a person seemed to know you.
questions.a: Could it be said of almost anyone? Did I give the answer away? How many guesses were wrong?
